notes: First IONQ 10-K post-SPAC (de-SPAC closed Sep 2021). Narrative leans on commercial cloud (AWS Braket, Azure Quantum, Google Cloud Marketplace) and co-development with Hyundai/GE Research. Two unnamed significant customers (>10% of revenue) in FY2021. The only named federal-program relationship in the filing is a research partnership with DOE/PNNL for barium-source miniaturization, plus DOE Isotope Program as a supplier. No named Pentagon Program Elements (PEs), no AFRL/DARPA program names, no named DoD prime contract. Risk language is generic ('our technology may be deemed a matter of national security'). This is a thin J-Book corpus at the 2022 cutoff because the company's narrative is not yet J-Book-load-bearing; defense exposure is structurally present (cohort metadata cites AFRL Rome FA8750 contracting history including AFRL Quantum Networking) but not disclosed as a material revenue contributor in this filing.

claims.claim_text: IonQ has a partnership with the U.S. Department of Energy's Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) under which it announced the miniaturization of the barium source material to a microscopic scale, which it characterizes as significant for shrinking core system components.
claims.subject: IonQ, Inc.
claims.object_value: named partner: DOE / PNNL; no contract value disclosed; presented as a research milestone, not a revenue contributor
claims.source_quote: For example, we recently announced that through our partnership with the U.S. Department of Energy's Pacific Northwest National Laboratory ('PNNL'), we were able to shrink the barium source material down to a microscopic scale. We believe this is significant because it will allow us to reduce the size of core system components, an important step in the creation of quantum computers small enough to be networked together.
